problem: The arrival time of the steepest guided ray is wrong. The zig-zag path is L/cos θ = L n₁/n₂, but light in the core travels at speed c/n₁, not c. So the time is (L n₁/n₂) × (n₁/c) = L n₁²/(c n₂). The printed t₂ = L n₁/(c n₂) is missing one factor of n₁ and does not give the ΔT formula printed just below it (subtracting t₁ = L n₁/c from L n₁/(c n₂) does not produce (L n₁/c)((n₁ − n₂)/n₂)).
fix: The ray zig-zags, so it covers the longer path L/cos θ = L n₁/n₂, and it travels that path at speed c/n₁. It therefore arrives at t₂ = (L n₁/n₂)(n₁/c) = L n₁²/(c n₂). Then ΔT = t₂ − t₁ = (L n₁/c)(n₁/n₂ − 1) = (L n₁/c)((n₁ − n₂)/n₂) ≈ L n₁ Δ/c, as stated.

problem: The note under the formula says "Both lengths must be in the same unit before you compare them." The formula contains no lengths, only times (the spread ΔT and the bit period 1/B). A student will look for two lengths that are not there and miss the real point about units.
fix: Replace with: "Both times — the spread ΔT and the bit period 1/B — must be in the same unit (both in ns, or both in s) before you compare them."

problem: The description says the step-index line "climbs fifty times faster" than the graded-index line. The slopes are 50 ns/km and 0.25 ns/km, so the step-index line climbs two hundred times faster. Fifty is the step-index slope in ns/km, not the ratio.
fix: "...the step-index line climbs two hundred times faster than the graded-index line."

problem: The lead says graded-index profiles shrink the spread "by about a factor of a hundred", but section 2 and worked example 1 show the improvement is 2/Δ = 200 for Δ = 0.01, and the chapter's own numbers (50 ns/km against 0.25 ns/km) give 200. The two figures conflict.
fix: Say "by a factor of about 2/Δ — roughly two hundred times at Δ = 0.01" in the lead, so it matches the rest of the chapter.
